category_title: Struggling readers supported by literal comprehension scaffolding
scenario_title: Scaffolding inference and justification for character motivations
minimal_context: The student and teacher are discussing a self-selected book about a pancake eating contest during a one-on-one reading conference.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's discuss your book. What happened during the pancake eating contest?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: He wanted to eat the most pancakes.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What did he do with the juice?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: He didn’t know that they could drink a lot of juice, more than him.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: How would you describe the way the character acted when he did that?

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's discuss your book. What happened during the pancake eating contest?

STUDENT: He wanted to eat the most pancakes.

TUTOR: What did he do with the juice?

STUDENT: He didn’t know that they could drink a lot of juice, more than him.

TUTOR: How would you describe the way the character acted when he did that?

STUDENT: They were silly.

task.content: Inferring character traits and justifying motivations regarding a pancake eating contest
task.learning_goal: Draw conclusions from the text and/or prior knowledge to explain some aspect of the story

context.materials: Self-selected books, SEM-R bookmarks listing sample questions

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When asked an inference question about how a character acted
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Provides a brief response without justification

behavior_patterns.condition: When responding to higher-level follow-up questions
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Requires heavy scaffolding to support claims or opinions expressed in response to a previous question or to draw conclusions from the text
